newsitem.title: GERMANY: RWE won't comment on report of writedown.
newsitem.headline: RWE won't comment on report of writedown.

text.p: RWE AG on Saturday declined to comment on a magazine report that it planned to take a charge of 700 million marks to reflect that some of its units were overvalued.
But the diversified German energy and telecommunications group said two of its subsidiaries may write down the value of firms in their books.
RWE also gave no comment on a claim by Spiegel magazine that it wanted Westdeutsche Landesbank (WestLB) to take a stake in RWE to replace local authorities which own about 40 percent.

An RWE spokesman told Reuters that two RWE units, waste management firm RWE Entsorgung AG and mining company Rheinbraun AG, were mulling writing down the value of several companies they had acquired, some of which were in east Germany.
He declined to specify the extent of the writedowns.
"We are thinking about taking measures in the individual accounts of RWE Entsorgung and Rheinbraun but these will have no impact on the group accounts," RWE spokesman Dieter Schweer said.
Spiegel reported that RWE Entsorgung had found it paid too much for several of the recycling firms it bought in Germany and eastern Europe over the last seven years.
The market for recycling had been overestimated, Spiegel said in an article released ahead of publication in Monday's editions.

Spiegel also reported that RWE chief executive Dietmar Kuhnt wanted WestLB to step in as a shareholder to facilitate a restructuring which will see the sale of loss-making units, the replacement of top executives and changes to RWE's accounts.
Some cash-strapped local authorities appeared to be ready to sell their shares, the report said.
Schweer said: "As a rule we don't comment on the activities of our shareholders."
He also described as "speculation" Spiegel's claim that the chief executive of RWE's Otelo telecommunications joint venture with Veba AG, Ulf Bohla, would be replaced in the autumn.
